scenario.title: Specification Document Review
scenario.initial_description: An engineer reviews a specification document to check whether new features are reflected correctly and whether there are typos or missing details.

reference_workflow.goal: Review a specification document for feature coverage, consistency, and editorial errors.

activities.name: Collect document and related change list
Compare feature changes with document content

automation_opportunities.rationale: Feature coverage can be checked by comparing change lists and document sections.
Terminology, formatting, and typo checks can be automated.
Review comments can be grouped by section, severity, and owner.

activities.name: Identify New Features in Change Log
outputs: List of new or modified features

activities.name: Cross-Check Features Against Requirements Source
inputs: List of new or modified features
outputs: List of missing or mismatched features

activities.name: Review Document for Typos and Language Errors
outputs: Annotated document with flagged language errors

activities.name: Check for Missing Details or Incomplete Sections
activities.system: Text Editor or Document Review Tool
outputs: List of incomplete or missing sections

activities.name: Compile Review Findings
activities.system: Document Management System or Issue Tracker

activities.name: Make Review Decision
activities.system: Issue Tracker or Document Management System

activities.name: Approve and Sign Off Specification Document

decisions.condition: Are all new features correctly and completely reflected in the specification?
branches: Yes — proceed to language and completeness review
No — flag missing or incorrect features for revision

decisions.condition: Are there typos, language errors, or missing sections found?
branches: Yes — include in consolidated review findings
No — document is linguistically and structurally complete

decisions.condition: Does the consolidated review report contain any findings requiring correction?
branches: Yes — submit revision requests to document author
No — approve and sign off the specification document

exceptions: Specification document version not found or inaccessible in the document management system
No change log available to identify new features (requires manual full-document comparison)
Requirements baseline is outdated or unavailable for cross-checking
Document author is unavailable to address revision requests within review timeline
Conflicting versions of the specification document exist simultaneously
Review deadline is missed due to document volume or complexity

automation_opportunities.target: A4 — Review Document for Typos and Language Errors
automation_opportunities.rationale: Natural language processing and grammar-checking tools can automatically scan specification documents for spelling mistakes, grammatical errors, and stylistic inconsistencies with high accuracy and speed, eliminating the need for manual proofreading.
constraints: Domain-specific terminology may require custom dictionary configuration
Tool must handle structured technical language, not just general prose

automation_opportunities.target: A5 — Check for Missing Details or Incomplete Sections
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated document structure validation can compare the specification against a predefined template or schema to detect missing sections, empty placeholders, or incomplete tables without manual inspection.
required_data: Standard document template or structural schema
constraints: Requires a well-defined and stable document template
Cannot assess semantic completeness, only structural completeness

automation_opportunities.target: A2 — Identify New Features in Change Log
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated version diffing tools can compare the current and previous versions of the specification document to extract additions, deletions, and modifications, reducing manual effort in identifying changes.
required_data: Previous version of specification document or structured change log
constraints: Previous version must be available and accessible
Unstructured or inconsistently formatted documents reduce diff accuracy

automation_opportunities.target: A3 — Cross-Check Features Against Requirements Source
automation_opportunities.rationale: If requirements are maintained in a structured tracking system, automated traceability analysis can match feature identifiers in the specification against requirement IDs to detect gaps or mismatches.
required_data: Structured requirements baseline with unique identifiers
Feature list with corresponding requirement references in specification
constraints: Requires consistent use of requirement identifiers in the specification document
Informal or narrative requirements are difficult to match automatically

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated aggregation of outputs from language checking, structure validation, and traceability tools can generate a consolidated review report without manual compilation, reducing effort and risk of omission.
required_data: Outputs from A3, A4, and A5 in structured format
constraints: All upstream tools must produce machine-readable output
Report format must be standardized and agreed upon

automation_opportunities.rationale: If traceability analysis produces a structured coverage matrix, the pass/fail decision on feature completeness can be automated based on a defined threshold or coverage rule.
required_data: Defined acceptance criteria for feature coverage
constraints: Acceptance criteria must be explicitly defined and consistently applied
Edge cases involving partial coverage may still require human judgment

automation_opportunities.target: A8 — Submit Revision Requests to Author
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated notification and ticket-creation workflows can route findings from the consolidated review report directly to the document author through an issue tracker or messaging system.
required_data: Consolidated review report in structured format
constraints: Requires integration between document review tooling and issue tracking system
Auto-generated tickets must be sufficiently descriptive to be actionable

assumptions: A document management system exists that stores versioned specification documents and supports retrieval by version or identifier.
A previous version or change log is available to support feature identification in A2; if not, a full manual comparison is assumed.
A requirements tracking system with a structured baseline exists for use in cross-checking features in A3.
A standard document template or structure schema is defined and available for completeness checking in A5.
The engineer performing the review is the same individual throughout the process; specialist roles (e.g., separate technical writer) are not modeled.
Review findings that require revision result in the document being returned to the author and re-entering the workflow from A1.
Approval and sign-off in A9 is performed by the reviewing engineer; escalation to a manager or review board is not modeled.
The review process is performed on a per-version basis and triggered whenever a new version of the specification is submitted.
Frequency of review is assumed to be event-driven (triggered by document submission) rather than periodic.
No formal regulatory or compliance approval is assumed beyond the engineer's sign-off, unless the scenario is extended.

missing_information.gap: No information on who performs the review — single engineer, a team, or a rotating role. Seniority or domain expertise requirements are also unspecified.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation scope and handoff logic depend on whether one or multiple actors are involved. Role-based routing rules cannot be defined without this.

missing_information.gap: The format, source, and versioning scheme of the specification document are not described (e.g., structured template, free-form text, wiki page, PDF).
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation feasibility for parsing or comparing documents depends heavily on whether the input is machine-readable and consistently structured.

missing_information.gap: There is no defined output artifact described — it is unclear whether the reviewer produces a formal review report, annotated document, ticket, or verbal feedback.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without a defined output, it is impossible to assess what automation could generate or route, and process completion cannot be detected.

missing_information.gap: No decision criteria are specified for what constitutes an acceptable specification versus one requiring revision. There is no defined threshold for typos, missing details, or feature completeness.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Automation or assisted-review tools require explicit rules or checklists to replicate or support human judgment at decision points.

missing_information.gap: No exception paths are described — what happens if the document is severely incomplete, if the reviewer is unavailable, or if conflicting feature requirements are found.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Exception handling is essential for end-to-end workflow automation; unhandled exceptions cause process breakdowns that block automation deployment.

missing_information.gap: The frequency and volume of reviews are not mentioned — whether this happens once per release cycle, daily, or on-demand is unknown.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Frequency and volume determine automation ROI and whether batch processing, real-time triggers, or scheduled jobs are the appropriate automation pattern.

missing_information.gap: There is no indication of upstream dependencies (e.g., who authored the document, what triggers the review) or downstream dependencies (e.g., what process is unblocked after review).
missing_information.why_it_matters: Without knowing triggers and downstream consumers, the workflow cannot be correctly modeled or integrated into a broader automated pipeline.

missing_information.gap: The time and effort required per review are not quantified — no estimate of how long the review takes or which sub-steps are most time-consuming.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Manual effort data is required to prioritize automation opportunities and build a business case for investment.

missing_information.gap: No systems or tools used during the review process are identified — it is unknown whether the engineer uses a document management system, diff tool, or issue tracker.
missing_information.why_it_matters: System identification is necessary to determine integration points for automation and to assess data accessibility.

missing_information.gap: There is no mention of whether the review outcome requires sign-off from a stakeholder or approval gate before the specification is considered finalized.
missing_information.why_it_matters: Approval gates affect workflow routing, SLA definition, and whether human-in-the-loop steps must be preserved in any automated solution.

clarification_questions.question: Who performs the specification review — a single designated engineer, a pool of reviewers, or a cross-functional team — and are there any required qualifications or domain expertise criteria for the reviewer?

What is the format and source of the specification document — for example, is it a structured template in a document management system, a free-form wiki page, or a PDF — and does it follow a consistent schema across reviews?

What is the expected output of a completed review — for example, an annotated document, a formal review report, a set of issue tickets, or a simple approval status — and where is this output recorded?

What criteria or checklist does the engineer use to determine whether a specification is acceptable, and how are findings categorized — for instance, by severity such as blocking defect, minor typo, or enhancement request?

How often do specification reviews occur, approximately how long does a single review take, and what triggers a review to begin — for example, a document submission event, a sprint milestone, or a manual request?
Is there a formal approval or sign-off step required after the review, and what happens when a document is found to be critically incomplete or when the reviewer is unavailable?
